title: Structure-Aware Abstraction of Hierarchical Time Series

problem.claim: Hierarchical time series abstraction seeks a small set of structure-aware subseries that jointly capture temporal dynamics and hierarchical organization.

gap.claim: Existing approaches either ignore hierarchy through flat clustering or overlook temporal similarities through hierarchical summarization.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates hierarchical time series abstraction as a problem of selecting structure-aware subseries.
It formally analyzes the problem, proving NP-hardness and showing that its objective is neither monotone nor submodular.
It designs a scalable greedy framework for constructing disjoint representative subtrees and proposes OSS with a 1/alpha-approximation guarantee for each single optimal-subtree computation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets and one large dataset reportedly show consistent improvements over strong baselines in representativeness and scalability.
A case study on the ACM dataset reportedly shows that HTSA produces concise, informative representations of complex hierarchical structures.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scalable abstraction of hierarchical time series must preserve effectiveness and efficiency.
Prior approaches fail to jointly capture hierarchy and temporal similarity.
HTSA is introduced as selecting a small set of structure-aware subseries.
The paper provides complexity and objective-structure analysis, then develops a greedy subtree-selection framework and OSS approximation procedure.
Experiments and an ACM case study report improved representativeness, scalability, and concise representations.

source_observation.claim: The abstraction objective must account for both temporal dynamics and hierarchical organization.

interpretation.claim: For structured temporal data, preserving only one structural dimension can produce incomplete summaries.

application.claim: Design summaries or representative subsets with explicit constraints for both temporal similarity and hierarchy.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design principle applies equally across all hierarchical time-series domains.

source_observation.claim: The objective is reported to be neither monotone nor submodular, while OSS provides a 1/alpha-approximation guarantee for a single optimal-subtree computation.

interpretation.claim: Approximation methods may need problem-specific guarantees when standard greedy objective assumptions do not hold.

application.claim: Expose an effectiveness-efficiency parameter when deploying scalable approximation procedures for complex structured objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the approximation guarantee for the complete multi-subtree framework or its dependence on alpha.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names beyond ACM, baseline identities, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the formal objective, algorithmic complexity, or approximation behavior of the complete framework.
The abstract does not provide implementation, reproducibility, or independent verification details.
